note: This ledger holds open work only. A finding that reaches 'closed' leaves this file in the same change that closes it, and its substance becomes an entry in CHANGELOG.md under the category it belongs to; the roadmap therefore shrinks as the programme advances instead of accumulating a tail of finished items. 'closed' is deliberately absent from states for that reason, and tools/verify-roadmap.php fails the build when an entry carries it. Every source anchor in this file was resolved against the repository at verified_at_sha. The 56 entries closed before this rule was introduced were moved to CHANGELOG.md with the commits that closed them.

findings.title: Record history can page across an ambiguous identity generation

source_anchors.note: Lines 1813-1829 on the verified SHA. historyByIdentityDigest() is called with $query->limit + 1 and $query->beforeVersion, then array_unique() over the returned page derives $recordKeys and refuses when count() !== 1. The uniqueness check is therefore page-local: a second generation outside the requested page is not observed.
Line 195. Applies the caller's limit and cursor to the SQL, so the repository never sees the full generation set.

findings.acceptance_test: A three-engine integration reproduction that creates a record under a public identity, produces multiple revision pages, hard-deletes it, reuses the identity for a new internal record key, and requests history with a page size that returns one generation. Before the fix it returns a page; after the fix the request fails closed on ambiguity regardless of page size, cursor direction or page position. Plus: page size 1, middle and last pages, reverse order, empty page, cross-site and cross-organization isolation, forbidden-record behaviour with no existence leak, hard-delete racing identity reuse, and stable errors on REST, CLI, MCP, administrator and portal.

findings.title: MCP transports a raw current password in published tool schemas and handler signatures

source_anchors.note: Declared at line 2057 and injected into three extension-lifecycle input schemas at lines 518, 535 and 552. writeOnly is set, which describes an output property and prevents nothing on the way in.

source_anchors.symbol: extension activate, disable and uninstall handlers
source_anchors.note: Thirteen occurrences of $currentPassword across lines 1439-1576, carried into ExtensionManager calls.

findings.acceptance_test: A recursive scan of the serialized MCP catalog that fails on any password, secret, private-key, recovery-code, token-value or raw package path field, wired as a test rather than a review step. Plus a handler-signature assertion that no MCP handler accepts credential material, and a documented safe alternative path for each lifecycle operation that previously used it.

findings.title: MCP destructive, credential, trust and installation-global risk taxonomy is incomplete

source_anchors.note: 76 tool declarations on the verified SHA. No declared risk class, and no validator rejecting a mutation tool without an operation identifier or an unclosed schema.
The single mutation guard the taxonomy must feed.

findings.acceptance_test: A central catalog validator rejecting duplicate tool names, missing handlers, incorrect annotations, unclosed schemas, mutation tools without operation identifiers, and any risk-versus-surface violation against the normative surface matrix. Every tool carries a declared risk class and a documented non-MCP alternative.

findings.title: The trusted-extension API boundary is not runtime isolation and must not be described as one

source_anchors.note: Curates service resolution. Admitted PHP still executes with the ambient filesystem, network, environment, database and process authority of the runtime user.

findings.acceptance_test: Documentation, administrator prompts and operator material all use the phrase 'trusted in-process extension code'. A test asserts recovery composition executes no extension PHP and reads no extension template or asset. An inventory of ambient authority ships with the deployment controls that bound it. Untrusted or marketplace PHP stays unsupported until an isolated runtime exists.

findings.title: Dependency direction is asserted textually, not enforced semantically

source_anchors.note: Four grep predicates: the product-name spelling, Symfony and Laravel as direct Composer dependencies, Symfony and Illuminate use statements, and two static-locator symbols. Nothing evaluates a layer graph.

findings.acceptance_test: An AST- or type-aware dependency checker implementing the layer graph from the Phase 0 architecture decision. Existing violations recorded with owner and expiry; every new violation fails immediately.

findings.title: BusinessRecordService owns too many use cases

source_anchors.note: 3,673 lines on the verified SHA, unchanged since the review's pinned revision.

findings.acceptance_test: Each extracted collaborator owns a coherent invariant, has explicit typed input and output, and is independently testable without duplicating application authorization or transaction policy. The facade's method signatures, errors, audit actions and event semantics are unchanged, proven by the existing cross-surface parity suite.
findings.product_owner_decision: Removed from the critical path. Only the seams the aggregate command and the scale work require are extracted, in phase 3. The remainder runs in lane M, parallel to or after scale work, and never blocks a gate.

findings.title: Application imports an Infrastructure-owned transaction port, and Doctrine adapters live under src/Application

source_anchors.note: Line 73. The same import appears in src/BusinessRecord/Application/BusinessRecordIdempotencyPurger.php:8, src/BusinessDefinition/Application/BusinessDefinitionService.php:23 and src/Application/Automation/AutomationManagementService.php:15.
A Doctrine adapter under src/Application, alongside DoctrineScheduler and DoctrineQueueRuntimeOperations.

findings.acceptance_test: The transaction abstraction is defined in Application or the shared kernel, adapted by Doctrine in Infrastructure, and Application receives no raw Doctrine connection or query-builder type through it. Commit, rollback, exception translation, retryable deadlock and serialization failure, non-retryable domain failure, nested call semantics, and audit and outbox atomicity are proven on all three engines.

findings.title: The definition-wide exclusive mutation fence serializes writes to unrelated records

source_anchors.note: Line 76. Acquires the schema-installation row with FOR UPDATE and holds it for the caller's whole record transaction.
Line 110. A shared fence already exists (LOCK IN SHARE MODE on MySQL, FOR SHARE on PostgreSQL) and is used by read paths only. It is the natural seam for the generation-aware protocol.

findings.acceptance_test: Two writers on unrelated records under one definition demonstrably overlap. Two writes to the same expected record version produce one winner and one stable stale-version error. A schema transition waits for in-flight writers and blocks new writers on the old generation. Rollback or crash releases or safely expires authority. Disable and trust revocation win without executing stale extension code. Success is measured as reduced lock-wait and transaction time at target load, not as different SQL text.

findings.title: A singleton projection event head is locked and updated inside the authoritative business transaction

source_anchors.note: Lines 140-181. A locking read of singleton_id = 1, then a guarded UPDATE of last_sequence, both inside the caller's transaction. Every event-producing commit contends on one installation-wide row.

findings.acceptance_test: Concurrent commits do not contend on the head row. A transaction that allocates then rolls back creates no visible event. A sequencer crash before or after range allocation is replay-safe and leaves no permanently missing event. Concurrent sequencers cannot duplicate or skip source rows. The sequence is monotonic and no projection checkpoint passes an unsequenced committed event in scope. Backlog sequencing reaches at least twice peak ingest with observable age and rate.

findings.title: No atomic multi-line document command

source_anchors.symbol: relate() and the single-line relation commands
source_anchors.note: A header plus N owned lines is expressed as a header mutation followed by N relation mutations, each with its own transaction, version, revision, audit entry, event and idempotency row.
The relational owned-line primitive already exists; what is missing is the one-command, one-transaction, one-version commit over it.

findings.acceptance_test: One generic vertical-neutral command atomically commits a 100-line and a 1,000-line aggregate with one authorization decision, one idempotent outcome, one transaction, one aggregate version increment, one revision identity, one audit action and one bounded aggregate event. Full rollback on any invalid or conflicting line. Exact replay returns the original result without rewriting lines, revisions, audit entries or events. The single-line relation APIs remain supported and unchanged.
findings.product_owner_decision: The contract is designed in phase 0 as an architecture decision record, before implementation, so extension authors build against the real shape from the moment Gate A opens.

findings.title: The seeded idempotency purge ceiling is two orders of magnitude below enterprise ingress

source_anchors.note: Line 60 seeds cron_expression '43 * * * *' and line 65 seeds payload {"batch_size": 500, "maximum_batches": 10}. That is 5,000 rows per hour, 120,000 per day.
Line 57. The batch is bounded to 1 to 1000 entries per call.

findings.acceptance_test: Maintenance throughput sustains at least twice the peak expiry rate while the ordinary workload continues, measured at the enterprise profile. Ingest rate, expiry rate, drain rate, backlog, oldest age and forecast-to-capacity are exposed as metrics. Enterprise readiness warns or fails when a required retention setting is absent or the drain slope predicts exhaustion.

findings.title: Durable gauges compute exact aggregates on the primary at scrape time

source_anchors.note: COUNT(*) at lines 208 and 227, MIN() at line 270 and MAX() at line 289. The statement count is bounded; the work of an exact count is not bounded by it.

findings.acceptance_test: Every durable gauge query is benchmarked at representative table size on all three engines. Any gauge exceeding its budget is replaced by a sharded incremental counter or an asynchronously reconciled snapshot, exposed as approximate while durable rows remain authoritative, with an operator-only exact diagnostic carrying an explicit cost and timeout.

findings.title: Integration fan-out executes every consumer and webhook serially in the dispatcher path

source_anchors.note: Line 91. Iterates executable event-consumer entries at line 106 and webhook entries at line 132 in the calling path.
The dispatcher the serial loop drives.

findings.acceptance_test: Independent (consumer, event) receipt rows are materialised in one short transaction and claimed in batches by worker pools. A slow, failing or rate-limited consumer does not delay unrelated consumers. Scenarios: fan-out 3 and 10, one hung consumer, poison payload, crash between claim and effect and settlement, generation change with queued work, retry storm, rate limit, downstream outage, and backlog recovery while new traffic continues.

findings.title: Declared-queue claims take a policy-row mutex and count live leases on the hot path

source_anchors.symbol: the queue-policy lock and live-lease count
source_anchors.note: Line 968 takes the queue_policy row with FOR UPDATE; lines 985 and 990 then run COUNT(*) over reserved rows with unexpired leases. The ordinary claim at line 270 already uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so the mutex is specific to contributed queues with a declared ceiling.

findings.acceptance_test: A configured queue owns durable concurrency slots claimed with portable leasing. One claim transaction may lease a batch where ordering permits. Completion, expiry, cancellation and recovery release the slot safely. No over-claim beyond declared tolerance, no starvation, bounded recovery after SIGKILL, and no site or organization able to monopolise worker capacity.

findings.title: Hot correctness ledgers have no enterprise hot-and-cold retention budget

source_anchors.symbol: the only shipped record-side retention schedule
source_anchors.note: Business command idempotency is the only business ledger with a seeded purge. Audit retention exists but is seeded disabled with a zero window (GM-AUD-07); revisions, outbox source events, sequenced journals, inbox receipts and job attempts have no declared budget.

findings.acceptance_test: Every hot store declares authoritative purpose, minimum retention, immutability, expiry index or partition strategy, hot and warm and archived state, batch and time and lock and replication budgets, its six retention metrics, backup and restore and legal-hold behaviour, and its failure and reconciliation procedure. Audit pruning happens only after a verifiable anchor is committed and the off-host archive is proven restorable.

findings.title: Coverage attribution and floor do not match the documented contract

source_anchors.note: 148 occurrences across 74 files on the verified SHA: 13 under tests/Unit, 36 under tests/Integration, 1 under tests/Functional and 24 under tests/Architecture. 314 test files use #[CoversClass]. Real BusinessRecord and cross-surface integration tests such as tests/Integration/BusinessRecord/BusinessRecordRuntimeIntegrationTest.php exercise behaviour without contributing attribution.
Line 271 sets coverage: 'true' on the PostgreSQL matrix entry only. Line 433 publishes the baseline with the text 'No threshold is enforced yet'.

findings.acceptance_test: Behavioural tests attribute the classes they exercise. Architecture and source-shape tests keep #[CoversNothing] only on a reasoned allowlist. The canonical full result is collected on MariaDB. Staged ratchets: no global decrease greater than 0.25 percentage point, at least 90% line coverage on changed executable PHP, at least 80% branch coverage on changed Domain and Application logic.

findings.title: The architecture-policy gate is four grep predicates

source_anchors.note: Invoked by composer architecture:policy and by composer qa. It checks the product-name spelling, forbidden direct dependencies, forbidden framework imports and two static-locator symbols. It reports 'Kumwe architecture policy verified.' without evaluating a single dependency edge.

findings.acceptance_test: composer architecture:policy runs a semantic checker as well as the textual predicates. Every new dependency-direction violation fails the build. Existing violations are recorded with owner and expiry and reach zero in phase 3.

findings.title: No single manifest defines the quality contract that local, CI, nightly and release runs execute

source_anchors.note: qa is a hand-assembled list: architecture:policy, docs:api, interface:programme, openapi:check, cs, analyse, test. security:audit and security:secrets are defined but excluded, and .github/workflows/ci.yml reassembles its own sequence.

findings.acceptance_test: One data-driven manifest defines the PHP and frontend contracts. CI, nightly and release consume it rather than reassembling it. Every command has one owner, purpose, expected artifact and maximum cadence. No hidden CI subset drifts from the local or release contract.

findings.title: The integration suite is not idempotent against a reused database

source_anchors.note: Added by 3fdb4e9 precisely because the class had been leaving the shared fixture database in a state later processes could not use. The suite has no framework-level guarantee of this property; the fix is per-class discipline.
Lines 16-18. No per-test database isolation, reset or teardown contract is declared.

findings.acceptance_test: The integration suite runs twice in a row against the same database with identical results, and runs in a different class order with identical results, as an executed CI step rather than an assumption. Any class that mutates installation-global state declares and executes its own rollback.

findings.title: No deployed-artifact test lane: four defects in the last programme were found only in production deployment acceptance

source_anchors.note: The only job that runs against the production image with the --no-dev authoritative classmap. Everything cheaper runs under the development autoloader with development dependencies present.

Added by 26a7b39 to retire the hand-maintained require list that had silently gone stale. The commit records the argument for this finding: 'the loss here was not the missing lines but a gate no cheap job covers'.

findings.acceptance_test: A lane that exercises the deployed artifact — production autoloader, --no-dev dependency set, read-only container, the real console binary — early enough to fail before a full deployment is stood up. The four defects it must reproduce as regression cases: the package-admission memory ceiling (cfaf840), the missing production autoloader path (26a7b39), the stranded record-encryption keys (3fdb4e9), and a drill leg that had never executed inside the deployed image (687707c).

findings.title: Browser and coverage depth is PostgreSQL-centric despite MariaDB and MySQL being primary

source_anchors.note: Lines 63-167. One PostgreSQL service, Chromium only. The three-engine matrix at lines 245-275 runs the PHP suite but not the browser journeys, and marks only the PostgreSQL leg for coverage.

findings.acceptance_test: Critical administrator, portal, generated-business, owned-line, maker-checker, step-up, policy-denial, no-JavaScript and website journeys run on MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL at merge. Nightly adds Firefox and WebKit, desktop and mobile, accessibility, keyboard, touch, high contrast, zoom and reflow. First-attempt results are reported separately from retry results.

findings.title: Scheduler dispatch joins two textual columns whose collation is not pinned, failing on a freshly created MariaDB database

source_anchors.note: Lines 140-141: 'INNER JOIN %s site ON site.identifier = o.site_identifier'. MariaDB raises error 1267, illegal mix of collations, when the two columns resolve to different collations.

Line 94 declares site_identifier as a plain Types::STRING of length 191 with no charset or collation copied from sites.identifier. Contrast src/Infrastructure/Persistence/Migration/BusinessSecurityPortalMigration.php:1188 siteIdentifierOptions(), which introspects the canonical column and reproduces its charset and collation precisely because 'relying on equal logical DBAL types is insufficient'.

findings.acceptance_test: A migration integration test that installs into a freshly created MariaDB database whose server or schema default collation differs from the one Doctrine resolves, then runs a scheduler dispatch pass and asserts it succeeds. The ownership column adopts the canonical site-identifier character definition through the same introspection the portal migration already uses.

findings.title: A foreign-key constraint name is hard-coded where MySQL and MariaDB treat the name as schema-global

source_anchors.note: Line 106 names the constraint literally 'fk_resource_site'. A second installation under one schema — a different table prefix, a parent-schema install, or a migration test reusing a database — collides with 'Duplicate foreign key constraint name'.
Line 443 already derives a unique name: 'fk_resource_site_' . substr(hash('sha256', $ownershipName), 0, 16). The two paths disagree, and the primary path is the one that collides.

findings.acceptance_test: A migration integration test that installs two prefixed installations into one MariaDB schema and succeeds. Every hard-coded constraint name in src/Infrastructure/Persistence/Migration is either derived from the table name or proven unique by that test.

findings.title: Release and distribution artifacts are not proven by one exact-SHA build-once chain

source_anchors.note: Artifacts are produced and scanned, but the published subject is not proven to be the identical digest that was tested.

findings.acceptance_test: The candidate SHA is proven to belong to the protected branch; each artifact is built exactly once; those exact digests are scanned, installed into empty directories, probed on all three engines and run together in the tested topology; and a signed qualification manifest contains every published digest, with published digests equal to tested digests.

findings.title: Point-in-time recovery is adopted as a platform-supported, operator-configured capability

source_anchors.note: Line 161 passes --set-gtid-purged=OFF on the MySQL leg, which strips the position marker replay needs. The MariaDB leg at lines 165-193 passes no --source-data or --master-data, so it records no binary-log coordinate at all. The PostgreSQL leg at line 149 uses pg_dump --format=custom, a logical dump that carries no write-ahead-log location and cannot be a base backup for replay.

source_anchors.symbol: Point-in-time recovery is a database-layer responsibility
source_anchors.note: The Wave 8 position, merged in 687707c: PITR is documented as the database administrator's and explicitly not owned by this repository.

findings.acceptance_test: Kumwe captures the backup coordinate on every engine (binary-log file and position plus GTID set on MariaDB and MySQL; write-ahead-log location and timeline against a physical base backup on PostgreSQL), records it in the backup manifest, ships restore-with-replay tooling that consumes an operator-configured archive, documents the procedure per engine, executes a drill that restores to a chosen point before and after a selected transaction, and enforces the media-versus-database ordering rule. The archive destination stays operator-owned.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D3. The Wave 8 position — PITR disowned as a database-layer responsibility — is superseded. Kumwe owns coordinate capture, restore-with-replay tooling, per-engine documentation, the drill and the ordering rule. The operator owns the archive destination. Restic is the documented reference off-site transport; Kumwe takes no dependency on it.

findings.title: Key-restoration order and encrypted-envelope restore proof

source_anchors.note: The documented eight-step order, the four excluded secrets and the permanence of each loss.

Added by 687707c. A restored operator authenticates, is allowed a read and denied an update, its session is accepted for its own user agent and refused for another, its restored TOTP credential passes a live challenge and is refused on replay, and recovery codes are reissued and spent.

findings.acceptance_test: The remaining open halves: approval spent state after restore, which needs an approval-rule administration surface first, and an HTTP replay of one login and one Idempotency-Key mutation against the restored container.
findings.correction_to_review: The review, pinned at 309db888, listed key-restoration order and post-restore proofs as incomplete. Wave 8 closed both — the documented order and an end-to-end envelope decryption through the production cipher — after that revision. Only the two named residuals remain.
findings.completed_reference: GM-BAK-02 and GM-BAK-03 closed in 687707c; their substance is in CHANGELOG.md.

findings.title: The backup artifact is shaped so that off-site deduplication cannot work

source_anchors.note: Lines 198-202 create four gzip-compressed tarballs: media.tar.gz, private.tar.gz, extensions.tar.gz and extension-assets.tar.gz. Compression randomises the byte stream, so a content-defined chunker sees almost entirely new chunks after any change and an hourly off-site snapshot re-stores nearly the whole payload.
Line 149 uses pg_dump --format=custom, which compresses by default. The MySQL and MariaDB dumps at lines 182-193 are already plain SQL text and need no change.
Restores the four archives and must follow the artifact shape change; the completion manifest and the .partial claim it writes are part of the contract that must survive.

findings.acceptance_test: Media, private, extension and extension-asset payloads are snapshotted as plain directory trees rather than compressed tarballs, and the PostgreSQL dump is taken uncompressed, leaving compression and deduplication to the transport. The existing sixteen fail-closed refusals in tests/Support/backup-tamper-drill.sh still pass, unchanged in meaning. A measured demonstration shows the stored delta of a second hourly snapshot after a small change is proportional to the change rather than to the payload.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D4.

findings.title: The media-versus-database restore ordering rule is stated as a trap, not enforced as a rule

source_anchors.symbol: Point-in-time recovery is a database-layer responsibility
source_anchors.note: Records the fact that no log covers the filesystem payloads, so a database rolled forward past the snapshot references media and export objects that are not there. It is documented as a fact to be aware of, with no rule the tooling applies.
kumwe-restore-manifest.json records per-tree path, file count and digests, which is the natural place to carry the payload snapshot instant that a replay target must not exceed.

findings.acceptance_test: The restore tooling refuses, or loudly records, a replay target later than the filesystem payload snapshot instant, and the drill exercises both the permitted and the refused case. The rule is stated once, in the operator documentation and in the tool, with the same wording.

findings.title: No runtime operational introspection: operators can see that the system is unhealthy but not where it is struggling

source_anchors.note: Wave 7 shipped monitoring: is it up, is it slow, is it erroring, is a queue deep. It did not ship diagnostics: which definition or policy is slow, which rows are contended, which queue is ageing and by how much, which retention stream is falling behind.
The monitoring contract the diagnostics must sit beside without duplicating.

findings.acceptance_test: An operator-facing diagnostic surface, distinct from monitoring, answering: lock waits and contention hotspots by table and statement class; queue depth and oldest age by queue; slowest definitions and policies by measured cost class; backlog build-up by stream with its drain slope; and whether retention is keeping pace. Bounded by the same cardinality discipline Wave 7 established: never labelled by site, user, record, event or document identifier, or raw route. Every diagnostic states its cost and carries a timeout.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D6.

findings.title: Accountable human acceptance of the interface standard remains unexecuted

source_anchors.note: composer interface:programme reports 42 surfaces, 85 templates, 23 navigation entries, 19 generated instances, 16 actors, 27 tasks, 13 journeys, 60 work items, 8 findings and 3 verification reports. The human gate is not among the executed evidence.

findings.acceptance_test: Named accountable reviewers complete the five archetype task journeys with task-based evidence. Automated Playwright, axe and visual results are necessary and not sufficient. Accessibility evidence covers WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard and focus and screen-reader semantics, touch targets, zoom and reflow, high contrast, loading and empty and error and denied and confirmation states, essential no-JavaScript flows, and reviewed visual regression on desktop and mobile.

findings.title: Programme state was spread across competing documents

source_anchors.note: 322 lines mixing an opening analysis, eight wave outcomes and per-entry closure prose. Its header still reads 'Gap totals: 0 critical, 13 high, 27 medium, 21 low' as an opening statement, which is no longer the current state of the programme.

findings.acceptance_test: docs/roadmap/ is the single authority for programme sequencing. The gap matrix is retained unmodified as executed evidence and says so in its own header. No second state database is created.

findings.title: The public extension contract is not classified or frozen, so it cannot be built against

source_anchors.note: AdministratorNavigation, AdministratorRoute, AdministratorView, AdministratorWorkspace, AuthorizationPolicy, BusinessDefinitionContribution, CapabilityDefinition, CustomBusinessActionHandler, CustomBusinessViewHandler, EventContract, FieldPresentation, FieldType, OwnedRuntimeContribution, PortalNavigation, PortalRoute, PortalTemplate, PortalWorkspace and ResourcePolicyDefinition. Nothing declares which of these, and which of the types they carry, are supported public contract.
The scaffolder an extension author starts from; the shape it emits is what a compatibility fixture must pin.

findings.acceptance_test: A machine-readable classification of public versus internal contract, plus executable compatibility fixtures: a representative signed package for every supported manifest and SPI generation that is still promised, which installs, activates, upgrades, disables, reactivates and uninstalls according to its declared compatibility contract. A later refactor is acceptable only if these packages still pass.

findings.title: A record invariant cannot aggregate over an owned-line collection

source_anchors.note: Lines 58-80. Twenty-one operators: literal, field, eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, and, or, not, add, subtract, multiply, divide, concat, coalesce, if, is_null, in, contains. There is no sum, count or any other aggregation over a collection.
Line 167 builds the evaluation scope with RecordExpressionValues::from($values), where $values is the record's own field values. Owned lines are not in scope.

Offers 'a total agreeing with its lines' as an example of what an invariant expresses. The vocabulary above cannot express it. The docblock overstates the capability and must be corrected whichever way the decision goes.

findings.acceptance_test: Core supplies a bounded aggregation over an owned-line collection: over exactly one declared owned-line relation, over exactly one line field, under the vocabulary's existing 32KB encoded ceiling and node-count discipline. A definition declares 'total equals the sum of line amounts'; a 1,000-line document violating it is rejected atomically with no partial commit and a stable named error identifying the invariant rather than the row; the evaluation runs once per aggregate command rather than once per line, proven by a query-count assertion so a per-line regression fails on the count rather than on a timing threshold; exact decimal semantics hold end to end, the sum of 1,000 ExactDecimal values being an ExactDecimal and never a float. A unit test proves Expression refuses an aggregation naming a relation the definition does not declare or a field the line entity does not carry. RecordInvariantDefinition's docblock becomes accurate in the same change.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D13.1 — core, and urgent. Without it every extension reimplements the most fundamental document rule differently and none provably.
findings.enforcing_check: Unit test on Expression's aggregation validation; three-engine integration test asserting atomic rejection of a violating 1,000-line document; query-count assertion proving once-per-command evaluation.

findings.title: Number sequences cannot be scoped by document type or legal entity, and reset only never, yearly or monthly

source_anchors.note: Site and Organization only.
Never, Yearly and Monthly only. There is no fiscal-period reset, and no concept of a fiscal period anywhere in src/.

findings.acceptance_test: The counter identity widens to include document type and legal entity, and the reset vocabulary gains a fiscal-period reset resolved through the PE-E period declaration. The allocator's advance mechanism is unchanged: only what the scope key and period key are composed from changes. Every existing gapless concurrency test runs unmodified against every new scope and reset combination — if one needs rewriting, the widening is wrong. A migration test proves every existing counter maps forward to exactly one widened counter with its current value intact. A widened scope means more counters each contended less, which is a throughput improvement obtained honestly; the meaning of an existing sequence is never changed for throughput alone.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D13.4 — core. Small, because the allocator already exists and already derives its counter row from a scope key and a period key.
findings.enforcing_check: Existing gapless concurrency tests run unmodified across every new scope and reset combination; a forward-migration test proving one-to-one counter mapping with values intact.

findings.title: No period-close or posting-lock primitive

source_anchors.note: Provides a per-record state machine with capability-gated transitions. There is no cross-record temporal lock — nothing that makes every record whose date falls in a closed range refuse mutation.

findings.acceptance_test: Core supplies a declarative temporal lock that refuses a mutation to a record whose declared date field falls inside a closed range, evaluated before the mutation fence rather than after it. Core gains NO fiscal calendar: what a period is, when it closes, who may close it and what re-opening means are the extension's, expressed through the lock's administrative surface. A three-engine integration test proves a mutation dated inside a closed period is refused on every surface, that closing a period is capability-gated and audited, and that a record dated outside the range is unaffected. Its interaction with V2-ERP-005 is a required test rather than an emergent behaviour: a correction issued after its original's period closed is dated in an open period, and neither mechanism special-cases the other.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D13.3 — core mechanism, extension policy.
findings.enforcing_check: Three-engine integration test of the refusal on every surface; an architecture test asserting the lock is consulted on every mutation entry point, enumerated from the same table the mutation guard already uses, so a new entry point that skips it fails.

findings.title: No unit-of-measure conversion and no currency conversion primitive

source_anchors.note: core.money pairs an exact amount with an ISO 4217 currency and configures precision, scale and currency; core.quantity pairs an exact quantity with a declared unit and configures precision, scale and unit. Both carry the denomination, neither converts. There is no rate table, no rate row, no rate provider, no conversion operator and no conversion service anywhere under src/.

States the limit itself: 'The unit is an opaque portable identifier — nothing here converts between units, so two quantities are only comparable when their units are identical.' The same is true of MoneyValue and is not written down anywhere.

Line 706 emits core.money as an exact decimal .amount column beside a fixed three-character ascii .currency column; line 710 does the same for core.quantity with a .unit column. Exact storage is already correct and this work must not alter it.

findings.acceptance_test: Core owns the typed value — it already does — and additionally owns the conversion contract for both money and quantity: the shape of a conversion request, the shape of a converted result, and the rules a conversion obeys. Extensions own the rate tables and the unit conversion tables. A conformance fixture proves an extension holds a conversion table and converts with no core edit, for a quantity in the mobile assignment fixture and for a money amount in the catalogue and order fixture. Stored exact values are untouched: MoneyValue, QuantityValue, ExactDecimal, the split physical columns and the pinned-denomination refusal are unchanged, and an architecture test asserts no src/ write path accepts a converted value where a core.money or core.quantity field value is expected.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decisions D10 and D13.5 — core owns the typed value and the conversion contract; extensions own the tables and the rates. Recorded in docs/roadmap/decisions/0004-money-conversion-contract.md. If core does not own the contract, extensions invent incompatible ones and cannot exchange data: a stock extension and a sales extension would disagree about what a case of a product is.
findings.enforcing_check: Construction and serialization tests proving the converted type cannot exist without its provenance; an architecture test proving conversion cannot leak into storage; conformance-fixture assertions for both the quantity and the money case.

findings.title: No immutable-correction primitive: an approved document is corrected by mutating it

source_anchors.note: Revisions record what changed, and the audit chain proves the record was not tampered with, but there is no declared 'this document is immutable after this transition; correct it by issuing a linked reversing document' primitive.

Line 130. Freezes one field from creation, which is a different rule from freezing a whole document from a transition. A document is mutable while it is a draft and frozen once approved; no existing declaration expresses that.

Supplies the per-record state machine whose transitions run only through an action whose capability the actor holds. The declaration the reversal model needs hangs here, so the mechanism is an addition to an existing shape rather than a new one.

findings.acceptance_test: A workflow binding may declare that entering a state makes the record immutable. After that transition every mutation of the record's own fields and its owned lines is refused on every surface, including surfaces an extension contributes, with a stable named error rather than a policy denial — the caller may be fully authorized; the document is closed. Correction is a new record of the same definition carrying a first-class typed link to the record it reverses, with its own approval path; the original is never rewritten and never suppressed, and both remain readable and in history. A 1,000-line reversal commits through the P4-A aggregate command; no separate reversal write path exists. Core knows nothing about what reversing means for a ledger or a balance. Definitions that do not declare post-transition immutability are unaffected, so nothing regresses for a definition that never opts in.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D13.2 — core. This is an audit property, not an accounting feature: a platform whose identity is auditability cannot allow an approved document to be edited. Recorded in docs/roadmap/decisions/0003-immutable-correction-by-reversal.md.
findings.enforcing_check: An architecture test asserting no mutation path in src/ can write a record whose definition declares it immutable in its current state, so a new write path cannot bypass the rule silently; a three-engine integration test proving update, owned-line mutation and archive are refused with a stable error on every surface and that the reversal path succeeds; a conformance-fixture assertion failing an extension that corrects by mutation.

findings.title: No role-specific dashboard composition primitive

source_anchors.note: A workspace is a navigation group with a label, description and sort weight. Its own docblock says it 'carries no behaviour of its own'. It is not a dashboard.
One fixed handler that filters its panels by the actor's capability map. There is no contributed-widget composition and no per-role landing selection.

findings.acceptance_test: Decide whether core gains a contributed dashboard-panel registry and a per-role landing route, or whether extensions ship dashboards as ordinary contributed administrator routes and views. If the latter, prove it in a conformance fixture and remove any documentation implying more.

findings.title: No offline-tolerant capture primitive for point-of-sale-style surfaces

source_anchors.note: No offline queue, no client-side durable store, no reconciliation or conflict-resolution primitive exists anywhere under src/. Client-supplied operation identifiers and the idempotency ledger give a retried command a stable outcome, which is the foundation an offline client needs but is not itself offline support.

findings.acceptance_test: Nothing is built for this in Version 2. What must hold is that Version 2 does not foreclose it: the four constraints in V2-POS-001 through V2-POS-004 are the entire residual, and this entry stays open until all four are settled so the deferral is a decision someone owns rather than an omission nobody noticed. The reviewer of any Gate A contract change asks whether it makes an offline terminal impossible; if it does, this entry is the place that objection is raised.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D14 — deferred beyond Version 2 as a product. Offline point of sale will be a separate long-standing application talking to the platform over the API. Version 2 does not build it and must not design in a way that forecloses it.
findings.residual: The platform must remain positioned to accommodate an offline terminal. That positioning is carried by V2-POS-001 through V2-POS-004, all of which are Gate A. This entry is the standing reminder that the deferral has a cost somebody is paying attention to.

findings.title: Money carries its currency but nothing converts it, so a price cannot be presented in another currency

source_anchors.note: Binds an ExactDecimal amount to an uppercase ISO 4217 alphabetic code, refusing anything that is not exactly three uppercase letters. The pair is the whole value of a core.money field. There is no second denomination, no rate and no conversion.

Line 977 compares a field's configured currency against a declared default with hash_equals(), so a field may pin exactly one denomination and refuses any other. That is a correct exactness control and it is also, today, the whole of the currency model.
Twenty-one scalar operators, none of which converts anything. There is no conversion operator, no rate table and no rate provider anywhere under src/.

findings.acceptance_test: Core gains the conversion contract: the shape of a conversion request, the shape of a converted result, and the rules a conversion obeys, plus the port a rate provider implements. Core ships no rate provider, no rate table and no rate policy. A product priced in one currency is presentable in another through the contract, and two extensions converting the same amount produce results with the same shape and the same provenance. Stored exact values are untouched: MoneyValue, ExactDecimal, the split .amount and .currency columns and the pinned-currency refusal are unchanged, and a diff of this work touching one line of them is a defect.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D10 — multi-currency is core. Core owns money-with-currency as a type and the conversion contract; rate providers and rate sourcing are extension and integration concerns, so an external rate service plugs into a pipeline rather than being wired into core. Recorded in docs/roadmap/decisions/0004-money-conversion-contract.md.
findings.enforcing_check: An architecture test asserting no src/ write path accepts a converted value where a core.money field value is expected, so conversion cannot leak into storage.

findings.title: A converted amount would be indistinguishable from a stored one, which is an audit defect rather than a formatting choice

source_anchors.note: Exports exactly two members, amount and currency, in the canonical shape used for storage, checksums and API output. There is nowhere in the value for a marker, a rate or an as-at instant to live, because nothing produces a converted amount yet.

Line 193 maps core.decimal to a report value type. Report and export payloads carry the value shape they are given, so widening the value is what widens the artifact; there is no separate provenance channel to add one to.

findings.acceptance_test: A converted amount is always marked as converted and carries the rate applied and the as-at instant of that rate, alongside the source currency and amount it was derived from. The type is constructible only in that complete shape, so an incomplete converted value cannot exist to be serialized. The provenance travels everywhere the figure does: the generated administrator and portal surfaces, the document view kind, report columns, export artifacts, the generated REST schemas, the machine surface and event payloads. A reader of a downloaded export can tell a converted figure from an agreed one without access to the system that produced it. A displayed price that silently drifts from its stored value is a qualification failure, not a rendering difference.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D10, the non-negotiable rule: a converted amount is always marked as converted and carries its rate and as-at instant. An operator must be able to tell, without asking anyone, whether they are looking at what was agreed or at what it is worth today, and if the latter, at what rate and as at when.
findings.enforcing_check: A unit test proving the converted type cannot be constructed without its rate and as-at instant; a serialization test proving the encoder emits all of them or fails, so a dropped field is a test failure rather than a rendering difference; a cross-surface test driven from one table of surfaces, so a surface added later without provenance fails rather than being missed; composer openapi:check for the generated REST half; and the capacity contract's undeclared_currency_conversions integrity objective at zero.

findings.title: No rate-provider extension point, so rate sourcing has nowhere to plug in

source_anchors.note: Twenty-four contribution methods covering capabilities, resource policies, workspaces, navigation, views, routes, field types, field presentations, business definitions, custom view and action handlers, event schemas, listeners, consumers, job handlers, queues, schedules, projections, reports and webhooks. None of them registers a rate provider or a conversion table, because no conversion contract exists for one to serve.

findings.acceptance_test: An extension registers a rate provider through the contribution registrar the same way it registers everything else, and a conformance fixture proves an extension can hold a rate table and convert without a core edit. Core takes no dependency on any rate source: an external rate service, a manually administered table, a bank feed and a contractual fixed rate are all implementations of one port, and none is wired into core. Which rate, from whom, applying when, rounded how and approved by whom stay entirely with the extension that owns the rate.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D10 — rate providers and rate sourcing are extension and integration concerns.
findings.enforcing_check: A conformance-fixture assertion in the catalogue, order and payment portfolio entry: an extension-held rate provider presents a price in a second currency with its rate and as-at instant, with no core edit. The existing extension-conformance runner is the gate.

findings.title: Reports and exports would carry a converted figure without the provenance that makes it readable after it leaves the system

source_anchors.note: Report columns carry the value shape the record supplies. A converted amount rendered as a bare number in an exported artifact is unreadable once the artifact is separated from the system that produced it, and there is no place in the current shape for the rate and instant to travel.
Exports are queued, stored and checksummed artifacts that outlive the request. Provenance omitted here is provenance lost permanently, because the artifact is the record the recipient keeps.

findings.acceptance_test: Report columns and export artifacts holding a converted amount carry the rate and the as-at instant as part of the value, so an exported artifact stays self-describing after it leaves the system. The export payload widening is stated in the work package and in the migration guidance rather than discovered by a consumer. A report combining stored and converted figures distinguishes them without the reader having to know which column is which.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D10. The audit rule is only worth stating if it is universal; a rule half the surfaces follow is not a rule.
findings.enforcing_check: The same cross-surface provenance test as V2-CUR-002, with report and export among the enumerated surfaces, plus an export-artifact assertion that a downloaded artifact carries the provenance inline.

findings.title: There is no translation layer at all, and every user-facing string is hardcoded English

source_anchors.note: AdministratorTwigEnvironment, SiteTwigEnvironment and RecoveryAdministratorTwigEnvironment, assembled by IsolatedTwigEnvironmentFactory. A grep for addFilter across src/ matches nothing on any of them, so no translation filter or function is registered on any surface. There is no catalogue format, no catalogue loader and no translator service anywhere under src/.
Every user-facing string is inline. templates/administrator/settings.twig line 100 renders 'Save settings and design' directly.
Console output text is inline in the command classes.
1,852 InvalidArgumentException constructions carry their text inline. Not all of them are user-facing, and separating the ones that are is part of the work.

findings.acceptance_test: A translator service exists, is bound into the Twig environments and the console, and resolves a message by stable semantic identifier. Every user-facing string on a translatable surface is looked up rather than written inline. Text that exists for a developer or a machine — a stable machine error code, an audit action name, a log line, a developer exception — is NOT translated, and the allowlist that says so names its reason per category: a translated error code is a broken contract.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — the interface is multilingual. Recorded in docs/roadmap/decisions/0002-interface-translation-architecture.md.
findings.enforcing_check: V2-LNG-007's hardcoded-string gate passing on a clean tree is the completion criterion for extraction. Extraction is finished when the check passes, not when someone judges it finished.

findings.title: The default_locale site setting is stored, validated and echoed, and consumed by nothing

source_anchors.note: Line 94 defaults it to 'en', line 284 reads it in validate(), and line 314 normalises underscores to hyphens and stores it. validate() refuses anything that does not match a language subtag with optional subtags, so the value is a genuine locale tag rather than free text.
Line 59 seeds site.default_locale as 'en'.
Line 97 is its only appearance in any template: it echoes the stored value back into its own form input. Nothing else reads it to select a language.
Line 2 hardcodes <html lang="en">, as do templates/administrator/layout.twig and templates/portal/layout.twig. No template emits a dir attribute or an hreflang link.

findings.acceptance_test: default_locale becomes the input to locale resolution rather than a stored string nobody reads. The three layouts emit lang and dir from the resolved locale instead of hardcoding en. A site whose default_locale is he renders right-to-left without any further configuration, and a site whose default_locale is unchanged renders exactly as it does today.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11.
findings.enforcing_check: A functional test asserting the rendered document element carries lang and dir derived from the resolved locale on all three surfaces, for a left-to-right and a right-to-left site.

findings.title: No authored catalogue format and no compiled runtime catalogue

source_anchors.note: No catalogue format of any kind exists. There is nothing to author against, nothing to compile and nothing to load.
openapi:check already proves a generated artifact matches its source, which is the shape the catalogue compiler's drift check reuses rather than inventing.

findings.acceptance_test: XLIFF 2.0 is the authored and interchange format, so a translator never opens a source file and an external translation platform or an AI-assisted pipeline connects through a format it already reads. The build compiles XLIFF to plain PHP array catalogues, so a runtime lookup is an array access served from the opcode cache with no XML parsing, no file I/O and no cache warm-up on the request path. XLIFF is never parsed at runtime. The compiled catalogue is generated output and is read before it is merged, like every other generated artifact this programme produces. The file layout core and an extension each ship is part of the frozen contract.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — XLIFF 2.0 authored, compiled to plain PHP arrays at build time.
findings.enforcing_check: A build check failing when a compiled catalogue drifts from its XLIFF source, in the same shape composer openapi:check already uses for the API contract.

findings.title: No message formatter, so plurals, gender, ordinals, numbers and dates cannot be expressed

source_anchors.note: Line 19 requires ext-intl unconditionally. It is a hard requirement already paid for.
Line 521 calls Normalizer::normalize(). This is the only use of ext-intl anywhere in src/. No MessageFormatter, NumberFormatter, IntlDateFormatter or Collator appears anywhere.

findings.acceptance_test: ICU MessageFormat, through the already-required ext-intl, formats plurals, gender, ordinals, numbers, currencies and dates. The reason is arithmetic rather than preference: the nine languages span one plural category (zh-Hans), two (the European set), three (he, which distinguishes a dual) and six (ar, which distinguishes zero, one, two, few, many and other), and the four-category Russian class is the next step outward. sprintf substitutes; it does not select. A test asserts correct category selection for each of the nine on a message with a count, including all six Arabic categories. Adding a four-category language later must be a catalogue change and not an engineering change.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — ICU MessageFormat via ext-intl, already a hard requirement so this adds no dependency. gettext is explicitly rejected: it depends on operating-system generated locales and setlocale() is process-global, which is unsafe in the long-running queue workers this platform runs by design, where one job's locale would still be in effect when the next begins. The argument is recorded in full in docs/roadmap/decisions/0002-interface-translation-architecture.md.
findings.enforcing_check: A unit test asserting plural-category selection per locale for all nine, and a worker-isolation test asserting two jobs processed in one long-lived worker under different locales each render in their own — the defect gettext would have introduced, proven absent.

findings.title: No message-identifier grammar, and using source text as the identifier would be irreversible once translation exists

source_anchors.note: Every contributed identifier is already namespaced by its owner, which is the pattern the message-identifier grammar follows rather than inventing a second convention.

findings.acceptance_test: A message is looked up by a stable semantic identifier, namespaced by owner. The source text is NEVER the lookup identifier. If it were, correcting a typographical error in English would invalidate that message in all eight other languages and every translator would redo work for a change that altered no meaning — irreversible in practice once real translation exists, which is why the rule is in the Gate A contract rather than in a style guide. The grammar refuses an identifier that is the source text, refuses an unnamespaced identifier contributed by an extension, and refuses an identifier differing from another only by case.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — stable, semantic message identifiers, never source text as the identifier. Part of the frozen contract at Gate A.
findings.enforcing_check: A unit test on the identifier grammar covering all three refusals, wired into the same gate that proves the catalogue compiles.

findings.title: No catalogue override chain, so an operator cannot change wording and a vertical cannot adapt terminology without forking

source_anchors.note: Site settings carry site_name, homepage_content_id, homepage_slug, default_locale, timezone, search_indexing_enabled and presentation. There is no per-site message override and nowhere for one to live.
An extension contributes through an owned registrar that namespaces what it registers. A catalogue contribution follows the same shape; today there is no catalogue to contribute.

findings.acceptance_test: Lookup resolves core, then extension, then site, then organization, last wins. Core ships the base catalogue; an extension may add and override its own and core's messages; a site may override either; an organization within a site may override again. Site- and organization-level overrides are stored in the database, so an operator changes wording through an administered surface with no file edit and no deployment. The strategic consequence is recorded in the operator and extension documentation rather than as a footnote: the same mechanism is TERMINOLOGY ADAPTATION — relabelling 'Client' as 'Patient', 'Learner' or 'Guest' for a vertical, in one language or in all nine, without forking core and without an extension shipping a parallel string table. An operator who does not know this will fork something.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — a four-step override chain, deliberately, because the fourth step is what makes vertical terminology adaptation possible without a fork.
findings.enforcing_check: A unit test asserting the chain resolves in the declared order and that a missing message falls back to the declared fallback locale and then to the identifier, never to an empty string — a silently blank interface is worse than an untranslated one. A performance test asserting the render path issues no database query and no file read per message, because an override chain that becomes a per-message lookup is a scale defect wearing a feature's name.

findings.title: Nothing would stop a new hardcoded user-facing string being introduced after extraction

source_anchors.note: The roadmap lifecycle check is the pattern: a test asserting it passes on the committed tree and a test asserting it fails, with a useful message, on a fixture that reintroduces what it forbids. The hardcoded-string gate is proven the same way.
The gap matrix rotted into a forward plan precisely because nothing mechanical stopped it. That is the argument for gating this convention rather than documenting it.

findings.acceptance_test: A check fails the build when a new user-facing string is introduced without going through a catalogue. It scans templates, console output and the user-facing error paths, and carries an explicit allowlist for the categories deliberately not translatable — machine error codes, audit action names, log messages, developer exceptions — with every allowlist entry naming its reason. A convention without a gate is a suggestion, and a translation programme protected only by review decays one merge at a time.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — enforcement is part of the decision, not an optional follow-up.
findings.enforcing_check: The check is itself the deliverable. It is proven in both directions: a test asserting it passes on the committed tree, and a test asserting it fails with a useful message on a fixture that reintroduces a hardcoded string. It joins composer qa.

findings.title: en-GB source extraction is unproven at the real surface area

source_anchors.note: The full template surface area extraction must cover.
Console output is a translatable surface; exit codes and stable JSON field names are not.

findings.acceptance_test: en-GB is the source catalogue and is extracted in full: every user-facing string in the 75 templates, the 47 console commands and the user-facing error paths of src/ has an identifier and a catalogue entry. This is the single largest mechanical change in the programme, and it is delivered at Gate A because if extraction does not work at scale then everything downstream of it is a guess. Only user-facing text moves; a developer exception, a log line, a stable machine error code and an audit action name are not user-facing text.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — en-GB extracted at Gate A to prove extraction works at scale; the other eight catalogues are Gate B.
findings.enforcing_check: V2-LNG-007's gate passing on a clean tree. Extraction is complete when the check passes, which makes completion an observable fact rather than a judgement.

findings.title: Right-to-left is unsupported, but the stylesheets are most of the way to direction independence

source_anchors.note: Counted at the verified revision: 16 logical inline-axis declarations (margin-inline, padding-inline) and 2 direction-relative alignments (text-align: start, text-align: end), against 20 physical margin-left, margin-right, padding-left and padding-right declarations, 11 physical border-left and border-right, 5 text-align: left, and ZERO floats. Right-to-left is a conversion of about three dozen declarations, not a rebuild.
Line 2 hardcodes lang and emits no dir attribute, as do the site and portal layouts.

findings.acceptance_test: Hebrew and Arabic are converted together, because the layout work is the same work and splitting it would mean doing it twice. The remaining physical inline-axis declarations become logical ones; the layouts emit dir from the resolved locale. Right-to-left gets ITS OWN visual-regression baselines: a right-to-left screenshot compared against a left-to-right baseline proves nothing. The P2-E matrix runs he and ar against those baselines with the same zero-horizontal-overflow and zero-inaccessible-critical-control acceptance as every other locale.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — Hebrew and Arabic are both in scope and are done together.
findings.enforcing_check: A stylesheet check failing the build on a new physical inline-axis declaration in assets/, with an allowlist for the cases where physical is genuinely correct and each entry naming why. Plus the per-locale visual baselines on the P2-E matrix.

findings.title: The eight non-source catalogues and per-locale qualification are unbuilt

source_anchors.note: Nine: en-GB (source), en-US, af, de, he, ar, es, pt-BR, zh-Hans. Traditional Chinese (zh-Hant) is not in Version 2 scope.

findings.acceptance_test: All nine catalogues are complete with no identifier missing that the source catalogue declares, and the browser, accessibility and visual matrix runs per locale with right-to-left carrying its own baselines. Zero horizontal overflow and zero inaccessible critical control in any of the nine. The proof-set sequencing is the point: en-GB, af, de and he first, because together they stress every hard axis — source extraction at scale, a smaller language with a thin tooling ecosystem, a layout-stressing language of long compounds, and a right-to-left script. After those four the remaining five are translation work rather than engineering work, and are scheduled and resourced as translation.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D11 — the translated catalogues for the nine languages and per-locale visual qualification are Gate B; everything that shapes a contract is Gate A.
findings.enforcing_check: A catalogue-completeness check failing when any of the nine is missing an identifier the source catalogue declares, so 'we shipped eight and a half languages' is not a state the build permits.

findings.title: Content carries no locale, no translation group and no per-locale publication state

source_anchors.note: Holds an identifier, title, slug, body, workflow state, publication window and version. Its own docblock enumerates what is deliberately absent — owning site, content type, workflow version, storage time — and no locale appears in either list. There is no translation group, no per-locale slug and no fallback declaration.
Line 313 writes a slug with no locale dimension. One entry, one slug, one publication window.

findings.acceptance_test: One logical item, one entry per locale: per-locale slugs, per-locale publication state so English may be live while another language is still drafting, and a declared fallback locale used when a translation is missing. A three-engine integration test proves a translation group publishes one locale while another drafts, that a missing translation resolves to the declared fallback, and that per-locale slugs do not collide across the locales of one group. Content translation is in Version 2 and is not deferred.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D12 — content is multilingual too, modelled as a translation group.
findings.enforcing_check: The three-engine integration test above, plus a slug-uniqueness constraint proven at the database level rather than in application code.

findings.title: Extension-contributed content has no way to declare locale variants, which is why the model cannot wait for Gate B

source_anchors.symbol: businessDefinition() and the view and template contributions
source_anchors.note: An extension contributes business definitions, administrator and portal views and templates, and custom view and action handlers. None of those declarations carries a locale dimension or a translation-group behaviour, because neither exists.
Contributions are checksummed as declarations. Widening a declaration after extensions are published against it is exactly the class of change Gate A exists to make unnecessary.

findings.acceptance_test: The translation-group model is part of the EXTENSION CONTRIBUTION CONTRACT, not only of core content. An extension contributing content declares its translation-group behaviour the same way it declares everything else, and a conformance fixture proves extension-contributed content gets locale variants with no core edit. This is the strongest reason none of the language work can wait for Gate B: an extension published against a contract with no locale dimension would have to be migrated.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D12 — content translation must work for content contributed by extensions, not only core content.
findings.enforcing_check: A conformance-fixture assertion in the extension-contributed multilingual content portfolio entry, run by the existing extension-conformance runner; plus P0-C's frozen-contract classification covering the translation-group declaration.

findings.title: Business definition labels are single strings inside an immutable checksummed document

source_anchors.note: Lines 148-149, each bounded to 120 bytes and validated at line 181. Both are members of the document exported at line 269 and encoded for the checksum.
Line 116 promotes the label; line 156 bounds it to 120 bytes and the description and help text to 1,000. All three are members of the exported document.

A published definition version is immutable and identified by a SHA-256 over these bytes, and package synchronization decides whether a declaration changed by comparing a stored checksum against a freshly encoded one. Adding a locale dimension after extensions publish would mean migrating live immutable documents.

findings.acceptance_test: Definition labels carry locales: EntityTypeDefinition's singular and plural labels and FieldDefinition's label, description and help text. Because a published version is immutable and identified by a checksum over the canonical bytes, the dimension must exist before the first extension publishes a definition. A checksum test proves a definition carrying single-locale labels encodes to the same bytes it did before the dimension existed, so no already-published version is invalidated by the change itself.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D12 — business definition labels carry locales, and because definitions are immutable versioned documents this is Gate A contract.
findings.enforcing_check: A byte-stability test on CanonicalDefinitionJson proving an unchanged single-locale definition produces an unchanged checksum across the widening; plus P0-C's frozen-contract classification covering the label locale dimension.

findings.title: No hreflang and no front-end language selector

source_anchors.symbol: the layouts and the site templates
source_anchors.note: No template emits an hreflang link and none renders a language selector, because there are no alternate-language documents for either to point at.

findings.acceptance_test: hreflang is emitted automatically from the translation group's members and lists exactly the published ones, so a drafting locale is not advertised. A front-end language selector ships by default rather than being added later, and it offers exactly the locales the group publishes. Both are proven by a functional test on the public surface.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D12 — automatic hreflang and a shipped language selector, by default rather than later.
findings.enforcing_check: A functional test asserting hreflang lists exactly the published members of the group and no others, and that the selector offers exactly those locales.

findings.title: The idempotency claim expires after a fixed day, so a terminal reconnecting later replays into a second effect

source_anchors.note: operationId is documented as 'the idempotency key the caller supplied, 8 to 128 characters', so the operation identifier is ALREADY client-minted. The scope digest is taken over site, organization, actor, operation and identifier, and the request payload and authorization context are fingerprinted alongside and re-checked before a replay is trusted.

Parses the client-supplied Idempotency-Key header once and publishes the validated value on the request. A missing header is answered idempotency-key-required and a malformed one invalid-idempotency-key, both 400, because neither is fixed by repeating the request.

Lines 2212 and 2325 construct the claim with new DateInterval('P1D'). Lines 2370 and 2431 treat an entry at or past expiresAt as absent. A terminal reconnecting after 24 hours therefore replays into a fresh claim and produces a second effect.

findings.acceptance_test: The contract states plainly who mints the operation identifier — the caller already does — and for how long a replay is honoured. The fixed P1D window becomes a declared, bounded, configurable retention with a stated maximum, and the contract says what happens to a replay arriving after it. What the actor component of the scope digest means for a terminal that re-authenticated while disconnected is stated rather than left to be discovered. A three-engine integration test proves a replay inside the declared window yields exactly one effect and a replay outside it is REFUSED with a stable named error rather than silently creating a second: the refusal is the property, and an implementation that quietly duplicates fails.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D14 — point of sale is deferred as a product, but a terminal creating a document offline must be able to mint the operation identifier itself and submit later, with replay yielding one effect.
findings.enforcing_check: The three-engine replay test above, covering both inside and outside the declared window, and covering a replay submitted after re-authentication.

findings.title: Numbering under disconnection: the gapless allocator commits inside the caller's transaction, so a disconnected terminal cannot call it

source_anchors.note: States it explicitly: 'this class opens none. It joins the transaction BusinessRecordService already has open around the whole create command'. It takes the counter row FOR UPDATE and holds the lock until that transaction ends, which is what makes a rolled-back create hand its number straight back. A disconnected terminal has no such transaction to join.

The shipped promise, stated exactly: within one counter the values handed to committed records are contiguous from one, with no duplicates and no gaps. Either candidate shape changes what that promise means, which is why this is a decision rather than an implementation detail.

findings.acceptance_test: Choose between two viable shapes and record the consequence of the one chosen. (1) Allocate the human document number at SYNCHRONISATION TIME: the terminal carries its own client reference until then, that reference becomes a declared field with its own uniqueness scope, and the number is allocated by the receiving command exactly as it is today, preserving gaplessness in full. (2) Issue PER-TERMINAL RESERVED BLOCKS: the terminal allocates from its own block while disconnected, which FORFEITS GAPLESSNESS for those counters. If (2) is chosen, the forfeit is declared on the sequence itself and stated in the supported envelope, never left implicit. This interacts directly with the gapless guarantee already documented and shipped, and that trade is the product owner's to make; it is not decided here.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D14 records the constraint and the two viable shapes and explicitly leaves the choice open. It must be taken in P0-E, because both shapes change the allocator and one of them changes a shipped promise.
findings.enforcing_check: Once decided: if synchronisation-time allocation, the existing gapless concurrency tests run unmodified. If reserved blocks, a test asserts a sequence declaring them reports itself as non-gapless through the same declaration an operator reads, so the forfeit cannot be silent.

findings.title: No declared home for a client-asserted occurrence instant, and no stated tolerance for late or out-of-order arrival

source_anchors.note: Takes a PSR ClockInterface and stamps one instant per command from it at lines 2187 and 2300. No surface accepts a client-asserted occurrence instant, so there is currently nowhere for one to live — which is the gap, not a protection.

source_anchors.symbol: the sequenced journal and projection checkpoints
source_anchors.note: Event ordering is by allocated sequence, and projections consume in that order. Nothing states whether a document captured days earlier and submitted now is ordered by capture or by arrival, because nothing yet arrives late by design.

findings.acceptance_test: A client-asserted captured-at instant has a declared place to live beside the server's own, is never substituted for it, and is never used for ordering, expiry, period assignment or numbering — a terminal's clock cannot be authoritative. Late and out-of-order arrival is accepted: a document captured on Friday and submitted on Monday is acceptable and is not ordered by when it arrived. Both are statements about the aggregate command's contract and about event sequencing, and both are tested rather than assumed.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D14 — late and out-of-order arrival tolerance, and untrusted client clocks.
findings.enforcing_check: An architecture test asserting no ordering, expiry or numbering path reads a client-asserted instant, enumerated from the paths that consume an instant; plus an integration test submitting a batch out of capture order and asserting the resulting order.

findings.title: Nothing states which validations may be deferred to reconciliation, so accept-and-reconcile is not a supportable posture

source_anchors.note: Every declared rule is evaluated at command time. There is no notion of a validation an extension may legitimately defer, and no statement of which validations can never be deferred.

findings.acceptance_test: The contract states which validations an extension may defer to reconciliation and which can never be deferred. Authorization, policy and definition-shape validity are never deferrable. Stock and pricing cannot be authoritative offline, so the design accepts a sale and reconciles rather than assuming live validation was possible at capture time. This is the one rule in the set that cannot be checked mechanically, because it is a statement about what an extension may CHOOSE; it is covered by the extension-contract review in P0-C and by a worked example in the extension documentation, and the work package says so rather than leaving the question silent.
findings.product_owner_decision: Decision D14 — stock and pricing cannot be authoritative offline, so the design must accept a sale and reconcile rather than assume live validation.
findings.enforcing_check: Not mechanically enforceable, and stated as such. Covered by the P0-C frozen-contract review, which classifies the deferrable and non-deferrable validation categories, and by a worked example in the extension documentation. The non-deferrable half IS mechanically enforced: an architecture test asserts authorization, policy and definition-shape validation have no bypass path.

findings.title: Append-only held only by application discipline
findings.acceptance_test: Triggers install where the server grants the privilege; where it refuses, audit:verify exits 2 and reports append_only_enforcement: not_installed, observed from the server catalog on every run.
findings.residual: On a managed service that withholds CREATE TRIGGER there is no database-level prevention of UPDATE or DELETE on audit_events. Tamper evidence, which is what the domain claims, holds unconditionally.

findings.title: Audit-metadata redaction is a write-time convention with no runtime guard

source_anchors.note: Stored verbatim; enforcement is per-service discipline. src/Audit/Application/AuditMetadataRedactor.php redacts on the way out of an export only.

findings.acceptance_test: A denylist decorator around AuditRecorder, or a constructor check, rejecting credential-shaped metadata keys and values, plus unit assertions on each writing service's recorded metadata.

findings.title: The administrator login form has no login-CSRF protection

source_anchors.note: Reads only email, password and User-Agent. The portal login already implements the pre-session double-submit token.

findings.acceptance_test: Mirror the portal pattern: set a path-scoped HttpOnly SameSite=Strict CSRF cookie on GET, render it as a hidden field, and hash_equals-compare and rotate on POST before authenticating.

findings.title: The session cookie Secure attribute has no production fail-closed guard, and there is no idle timeout

source_anchors.note: Secure is derived solely from the configured base-URL scheme. last_seen_at is stamped but never used in the resolve predicate.

findings.acceptance_test: Production configuration refuses a base URL that would serve session cookies without Secure. An idle-window predicate is added to the resolve path or its absence is stated as a deliberate, documented property.

findings.title: Qualification evidence has session and CSRF test blind spots

source_anchors.note: No dedicated comparison or rejection tests. No test anywhere asserts the session cookie attribute string.

findings.acceptance_test: Dedicated tests for both CSRF middlewares, the Redis rate-limiter window arithmetic, the portal session store find and rotate rejection matrix, the logout handlers, and the session cookie attribute string.

findings.title: Self-service credential rotation is reachable only by holders of users.manage

source_anchors.note: Both verbs are gated on users.manage. The portal has a security screen but no password path at all.

findings.acceptance_test: An ordinary portal member and a narrowly scoped administrator can rotate their own password without an identity administrator performing a reset.

findings.title: Out-of-process execution for untrusted code is a documented invariant without a shipped runtime

source_anchors.note: Curation covers service resolution only. Admitted PHP executes with the ambient authority of the process.

findings.acceptance_test: Cannot be closed by repository-owned code. Until an isolated runtime exists, installing an extension means trusting its publisher with the application process, and the documentation, UI and operator prompts must all say exactly that.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy admitted unsafe-inline for styles on every response

source_anchors.note: Now style-src 'self', style-src-elem 'self' and style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline' in place of one permissive directive.

findings.acceptance_test: The exfiltration class is removed. The narrowed residual — inline style attributes — is named and owned.

findings.title: The per-commit source SBOM is short-retention CI evidence nothing consumes

source_anchors.note: 14-day artifact retention; no workflow step reads it.

findings.acceptance_test: A license-and-policy evaluation over the CycloneDX output, and publication as a build attestation or with longer retention. Blocked on a license policy nobody has agreed; a gate over an undecided policy would be scanning theatre.
findings.forward_reference: V2-REL-001 is the natural home for this once the build-once chain exists.

findings.title: No distributed tracing and no trace exporter

source_anchors.note: Exporter none, sampling declared. W3C trace-context propagation exists and must not be overstated as distributed tracing.

findings.acceptance_test: Open by decision. Adopting an exporter is a separately reviewed dependency and configuration decision. Until then, documentation states propagation, never tracing.

findings.title: Post-restore identity and security acceptance was manual
findings.acceptance_test: Still open: approval spent state, which needs an approval-rule administration surface first, and an HTTP replay of one login and one Idempotency-Key mutation against the restored container.

findings.title: Backup scheduling, retention and off-host copy are operator-owned, and whole-table parity is not asserted
findings.acceptance_test: Documented: a reference hourly timer and unit, the four-step cycle, a retention prune that refuses to empty the directory, and an explicit list of what stays operator-owned. Open by choice: whole-table row-count parity is not in the acceptance manifest.
findings.forward_reference: V2-DR-003 changes the artifact this section documents; the reference schedule and the off-host step must be restated for the reshaped payload and the reference transport.
